preamble: Raising and diphthongization of /æ/ to [eɪ] is documented as a conditioned change in North American English: before the velars /ɡ/ and /ŋ/, the velar 'pinch' raises the tongue body and adds a palatal up-glide, giving hang [heɪŋ] and thank [θeɪŋk]. In Wisconsin, Minnesota and Central Canada /æɡ/ has been reported to merge with /eɪɡ/ (haggle = Hegel). The same pre-velar raising occurs more weakly across the Upper Midwest, much of Canada and the Pacific Northwest. No comparable case outside English has been found.

languageExamples.language: North American English (Upper Midwest, Central Canada)

examples.note: Labov, Ash & Boberg (2006, p. 181) report a merger of /æ/ with /eɪ/ before /ɡ/ in Wisconsin, Minnesota and Central Canada.

Pre-velar raising with an up-glide; ultrasound data show the tongue body raised and fronted in /æɡ/ for speakers in Canada and the North-Central and Northwestern US, though not always reaching full /eɪ/.
The same pre-velar raising applies before /ŋ/ in much of Canada and the North-Central and Northwestern United States.

sources: Labov, W., Ash, S., & Boberg, C. (2006). The Atlas of North American English: Phonetics, Phonology and Sound Change. Mouton de Gruyter. https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110167467
